# Verify a tiny program as a Wasm component under a WASI host
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #345, sha256:2d14c1b7fc678b76d2db1861ce23a05d0df11f05a4bcf98d1f9c3603cc279e89). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** story
- **Repository:** avowry (compiler; source map and trace, today C# method names and a .NET build-id check)
- **Source:** .mob/records/platform-options/standalone-recommendation-2026-11-08.md (Proposed stories (PM), card 345) and the product owner's decisions of 2026-11-08 (stand-alone platform report: card 345 ranks ahead of card 346; Avowry is its own language; C# is the first adapter; Dana stays target-agnostic; Ari's execution constraint applied).
- **Depends on:** card 344 and card 360 (Avowry evaluates a program's specs itself: the WASI spec run needs that runner)
- **Story:** As Ari, I want one tiny program (a leaf, a failure, a spec) compiled to a Wasm component and its specs run under a WASI host, with a failure traced to its spec line, so that I can verify code inside a sandbox with no language runtime.
- **Consumer value:** Ari verifies that tiny program inside a sandbox with no language runtime; we see it when Wasmtime runs the specs and a forced failure names the spec line.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Scenario: [Z][S] specs pass with no language runtime
     Given Ari usually runs in a Linux container or sandbox and often cannot run code at all, and one tiny Avowry program (a leaf, a failure, a spec) compiled to a Wasm component
     When its specs run on Wasmtime
     Then they pass
  2. Scenario: [O][E] a forced failure names the spec line
     Given a forced failure in that program
     When the failure is traced
     Then the message names the spec line
  3. Scenario: [I] WASI host loads the component
     Given that Wasm component
     When Ari invokes the WASI host
     Then the host loads it and runs the specs with no Python, TypeScript or .NET runtime on that host
  Letters that do not apply: [M] this card is one tiny program; [B] HTTP, persistence and the component model depend on host support the seats could not verify.
- **Not in this card:** shipping a general Wasm target; a Wasm build of the toolchain (parked until this feasibility has run); card 346–card 349; publishing; a registry; a language server; a UI; other targets.
- **Unknowns:** what emits the Wasm; whether the host is bundled or a separate tool; the Wasm source-map shape (this card forces map and trace to become target-neutral); whether a .NET-to-Wasm/WASI path exists and is mature; WASI HTTP and component-model support in Wasmtime or Wasmer. A spike is allowed only once card 345 is the top story.
- **Size:** L
